title: Anchor analysis to the exact time period specified
when_to_use: The task instruction specifies a particular reference date or time window (e.g., 'latest month', 'June 2024').
experience:
- At the start of analysis, explicitly identify the exact time period required for filtering and reporting.
- Before applying any screening criteria, filter the dataset to this specific period.
- Perform all primary analyses (e.g., identifying unhealthy campaigns, computing benchmarks) on this anchored subset first.
- When performing time-series comparisons (e.g., YoY), ensure the baseline period is correctly aligned with the specified reference period.
- Clearly label all outputs to indicate the reference period used.
checklist: Identify the reference period in the task
Filter data to that period before screening
Use this period to compute benchmarks and targets
Align trend comparisons (e.g., YoY) to this anchor
common_failure_prevented: Using an overly broad time filter (e.g., all months) which dilutes results and fails to identify the specific entities of interest for the required period.

title: Verify and implement the precise calculation method for key metrics
when_to_use: The task or rubric defines a specific formula, imputation rule, or aggregation method for a critical metric.
experience:
- Extract the exact formula or rule (e.g., 'impression-weighted average', 'use 2024-Q2 mean for imputation') from the requirements.
- Before coding, write out the calculation logic in pseudo-code to confirm alignment.
- For imputation or handling of missing/extreme values, explicitly define the source of the replacement value (e.g., segment average, fixed threshold).
- Test the calculation on a small sample to verify outputs match expected anchor values if provided.
- Document any deviations from the specified method and the rationale.
checklist: Extract and document the precise formula
Define the source for imputation values
Compare results to provided anchor points if available
common_failure_prevented: Using a generic or different calculation method (e.g., simple average vs. impression-weighted average) leading to inaccurate metrics and failing rubric checks.

title: Structure multi-dimensional analysis at the correct entity level
when_to_use: The task requires comparing performance across dimensions (e.g., device, geo) for a specific subset of entities (e.g., high-risk campaigns).
experience:
- First, isolate the target entity subset (e.g., problematic campaigns for the latest month).
- For each analysis dimension (device, geo, etc.), join the subset's data with the dimension-specific data at the appropriate grain.
- Compute dimension-level metrics (e.g., cost share, ROAS) specifically for the target subset, not for the entire dataset.
- Summarize results per target entity (e.g., for each campaign, list its top 3 inefficient geo targets).
- Avoid aggregating across all entities first, as this obscures the per-entity insights required.
checklist: Isolate the target entity subset first
Join dimension data at the correct grain for this subset
Compute dimension metrics per target entity
Summarize findings at the per-entity level
common_failure_prevented: Performing aggregate-level dimensional analysis (e.g., average health score per device type across all campaigns) instead of campaign-specific analysis, missing the required per-entity breakdown.
